'Far from forgettable', 'no slouches' and 'wouldn't say no to coming back' are all positive understatements, so sentiment is positive and the reviewer would return.
'No small feat' means a significant, hard accomplishment and 'not unlike a staff engineer' is praise, so the feedback is positive and the achievement difficult.
Negative-in-effect understatements ('far from cheap', 'not exactly what was promised', 'won't be rushing back') mean an expensive, disappointing stay: negative sentiment, poor value.
'Not exactly modest' burn (4x revenue) means high, 'hardly seasoned' means inexperienced, and the note explicitly passes.
Two double negatives: 'can't say I'm not tempted' means tempted, and 'not going to turn down your offer' plus signing Monday means the offer is accepted.
Double negations 'nobody was unconvinced' and 'none thought she was unprepared' resolve to everyone convinced and the candidate prepared.
'Wouldn't call it bug-free' means it has bugs (two named: export timeouts, filter resets), and 'not useless, I open it every morning' means regular use.
'Far from worn out after 200 km' signals good durability and 'wouldn't say no to a second pair' means they'd buy again; the weight caveat doesn't flip the positive verdict.
'Hardly a disaster' and 'not a shabby showing' are positive understatements; the slipped launch is a distractor and only two launches were on time.
'Four is not undeserved' means the reviewer awards four stars, and the other understatement ('not unpleasant to clean') is mildly positive.
Control: 'not good' and 'would not recommend' are literal negations, not litotes, so sentiment is negative and the recommendation false.
Control: 'did not ship' is a plain negation (shipped=false), not an understatement to be softened; the blocker is a data-loss bug.
